title: Cross-engagement knowledge-base entry
description: One mechanism, two entry kinds (Workstream B.1). An entry REORDERS routing and annotates it. It never removes a route, never kills a candidate, never lowers a verdict (D-09).

kind.description: winner = a route that produced a confirmed finding. loser = a route we worked and closed.

engagement.description: Source engagement id. Omit when the source is under a disclosure obligation.

mechanism_class.description: Abstract mechanism, scrubbed. Never a target identifier.

family.description: Routing families this entry bears on.

cards.description: Card ids this entry bears on.

transfer_scope.description: Rule 2. How far this generalises. Without it a Backstage result would wrongly suppress a Kubernetes route.

applies_to.description: The concrete values transfer_scope is checked against.

boundedness.description: Rule 3. bounded = the space was exhausted. abandoned = we ran out of budget. They mean different things to the next run.

control.description: Rule 1. REQUIRED for kind=loser. A control is NAMED and EVIDENCED, never asserted. 'We looked and found nothing' cannot produce an evidence ref -- that is the point: a computable gate, not a length check.

mechanism.description: How the control holds, in mechanism terms.

evidence.description: file:line, record ref, or attempt id. Scrubbed.

control_is_proven.description: B.2 edge case. true = a demonstrated control (a fact about the target). Earns a stronger annotation, never kill authority: a control is version-specific and may have changed.

reopen_on.description: The materially new mechanism that reopens this. The family-registry reopen rule applies unchanged.

writer.description: B.4. Self-reported learning is the shape that produced the fabricated status field, so the write path is recorded.

ablation_fixture.description: Path to the fixture proving this entry changes a routing decision (B.3).
